title: Deletion gives the restricted metric and length additivity at a shortest parabolic coset representative
statement: Let $G$ be a group, meaning a set with associative multiplication, identity $1$ and two-sided inverses. Let $I$ be a finite set [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set] and $i\mapsto t_i$ an injective family of nonidentity elements generating $G$, with $t_i^2=1$. For a finite word $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ in $I$ put $t_A=t_{a_1}\cdots t_{a_k}$, with empty product $1$, and define $\ell(g)=\min\{|A|:t_A=g\}$. Assume deletion: every word $A$ with $|A|>\ell(t_A)$ has two distinct positions whose simultaneous removal preserves its product. For any subset $J\subseteq I$ let $H_J=\{t_A:A\text{ is a finite word in }J\}$; it is the subgroup generated by the $t_j$ for $j\in J$. For $u\in H_J$ define $\ell_J(u)=\min\{|A|:A\text{ is a word in }J,\ t_A=u\}$. Then $\ell_J(u)=\ell(u)$ for every $u\in H_J$. If $h\in G$ satisfies $\ell(h)\le\ell(vh)$ for every $v\in H_J$, then $$\ell(uh)=\ell_J(u)+\ell(h)\qquad(u\in H_J).$$ Empty $J$ and the trivial group are allowed. No presentation of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Cashen, Notes on Coxeter groups, version 31 October 2023, Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5 (Bridge Lemma), printed p.118, and Lemma 4.0.14(2), printed pp.120–121. Local copy WANTED; author-hosted PDF read online. Only the deletion argument is used, without assuming a Coxeter presentation. No Stacks tag states this abstract group fact.

proof.text: Products of words in $J$ are closed under multiplication by concatenation, contain $1$ through the empty word, and are closed under inverses: $t_A^{-1}=t_{\operatorname{reverse}(A)}$ because every $t_j^{-1}=t_j$. Thus $H_J$ is the asserted subgroup. Similarly generation by the involutions ensures that every element of $G$ has a word in $I$. The nonempty sets of possible lengths have least elements in $\mathbf N$, so all minima in the statement are attained.

source.place: Elementary setup for the one-sided specialization of Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5; written by NE from the explicit word definitions. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted version checked online.

proof.text: Fix $u\in H_J$ and choose a $J$-word $A$ of length $n=\ell_J(u)$. Since $A$ is also an $I$-word, $\ell(u)\le n$. If $\ell(u)<n$, the assumed deletion removes two positions from $A$ without changing $u$. The remaining word still uses only $J$ and has length $n-2<n$, contradicting the choice of $A$. Therefore $\ell(u)=n=\ell_J(u)$.

source.place: Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5, opening choice of a minimal tuple in the subgroup alphabet; direct deletion justification written by NE. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted version checked online.

proof.text: Now assume $h$ has the stated minimality. For arbitrary $u\in H_J$ choose $A$ as above and a shortest $I$-word $B$ for $h$; put $m=|B|=\ell(h)$. The concatenation $AB$ represents $uh$, so $\ell(uh)\le n+m$. If this inequality is strict, deletion gives two distinct positions in $AB$ whose removal preserves its product. We rule out all three possible locations of this pair.

source.place: Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5, first paragraph of proof, with the right subgroup empty; compare Lemma 4.0.14(2). Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted version checked online.

proof.text: If both positions lie in $A$, write $A_2$ for the resulting $J$-word. The equality $t_{A_2}h=uh$ gives $t_{A_2}=u$ by right cancellation. But $|A_2|=n-2<n=\ell_J(u)$, a contradiction. If both lie in $B$, write $B_2$ for its remaining word. Then $u t_{B_2}=uh$ gives $t_{B_2}=h$ by left cancellation, contradicting $|B_2|=m-2<m=\ell(h)$. Each case necessarily has at least two positions in the relevant block.

source.place: Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5, exclusion of two deleted entries in a single block; cancellations written out by NE. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted version checked online.

proof.text: The remaining case deletes one position from each block, leaving a $J$-word $A_1$ and an $I$-word $B_1$, with $|B_1|=m-1$ and $t_{A_1}t_{B_1}=uh$. Hence $t_{B_1}=v h$ for $v=(t_{A_1})^{-1}u\in H_J$. Minimality of $h$ gives $m=\ell(h)\le\ell(vh)=\ell(t_{B_1})\le |B_1|=m-1$, a contradiction. Here $m\ge1$ because a position of $B$ was deleted. Thus no deletion pair is possible, the strict inequality in step 3 is impossible, and $\ell(uh)=n+m=\ell_J(u)+\ell(h)$.

source.place: Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5, exclusion of a deletion in the minimal middle block, with the right subgroup empty; left-coset equation written out by NE. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted version checked online.

lean.statement: theorem deletion_parabolic_coset_length {G : Type u} [Group G] {I : Type v} [Finite I] (t : I → G) (hinj : Function.Injective t) (hne : ∀ i : I, t i ≠ 1) (hinvol : ∀ i : I, t i ^ 2 = 1) (hgen : Subgroup.closure (Set.range t) = ⊤) (hdelete : ∀ A : List I, generatorWordLength t (A.map t).prod < A.length → ∃ a b : ℕ, a < b ∧ b < A.length ∧ (((A.eraseIdx b).eraseIdx a).map t).prod = (A.map t).prod) (J : Set I) : (∀ u : G, u ∈ Subgroup.closure (t '' J) → generatorWordLength (fun j : J ↦ t j) u = generatorWordLength t u) ∧ (∀ h : G, (∀ v : G, v ∈ Subgroup.closure (t '' J) → generatorWordLength t h ≤ generatorWordLength t (v * h)) → ∀ u : G, u ∈ Subgroup.closure (t '' J) → generatorWordLength t (u * h) = generatorWordLength (fun j : J ↦ t j) u + generatorWordLength t h)
